evals.prompt: Review Code Quality & Go Idioms for this Go 1.27 library change. LookupUser(id) calls an internal SQL repository. On error it does `log.Printf("lookup: %v", err); return User{}, fmt.Errorf("lookup user %q: %w", id, err)`. The package promises callers only ErrNotFound and ErrUnavailable; callers already log returned failures. The error text can include SQL details. No other code changed.
evals.expected_output: A supported low grade identifying duplicate logging, an unintended unwrapping contract, and the fact that changing %w to %v alone would not remove sensitive error text. Suggestions should preserve a stable public error meaning.
assertions: The report identifies logging the same failure twice as a consequence of the shown caller behavior.
The report explains that %w exposes the internal error for errors.Is or errors.As.
The report does not claim that %v sanitizes SQL error text.
Each bad finding has a targeted change and rationale.

assertions: The report treats the empty slice as correct for the documented JSON contract.
The report recognizes the supported readability improvement.
The report does not claim []string{} necessarily causes a heap allocation.

evals.prompt: Review Code Quality & Go Idioms for a complete supplied area. login.go:20, refresh.go:30 and exchange.go:40 repeat the same short access/refresh token construction sequence, taking expiry and JTI directly from the session. The maintained contract requires that pair to use the same session values; a source trace shows changing this shared issuance rule requires repeating the small edit in each function. All three are maintained by the same API owner and currently agree; no hidden interactions, different classifications, caller failures or independently evolving policy owners are established. Browser cookie creation is a separate step only where needed. retry.go:10 has a local stopRetry boolean that is true when retrying; its eight-line helper has an explanatory comment, correct branches and tests. A reviewer calls both moderate because future edits might introduce a bug. Assess only this evidence.
evals.expected_output: B+ for two minor causes: a small synchronized policy edit and local naming inversion. The hypothetical future bug does not establish moderate impact. Retain genuine maintenance findings and propose proportionate changes.
assertions: Counts two minor causes rather than promoting either to moderate from hypothetical future mistakes.
Explains the bounded repeated edit and local semantic inversion as current maintenance/reading costs.
Keeps browser-specific cookie handling separate from any shared token-pair helper.
Does not require a general Client hierarchy or broad issuance redesign.
